title: Innovation
coreMove: Import useful patterns from elsewhere, recombine them under pressure, and cut until the new fit is real.
sourcePressure: The chapter uses idea brokers, creative desperation, and Disney's Frozen to argue that innovation is transfer plus hard revision, not isolated originality.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating innovation as pure originality, brainstorming volume, or deadline magic.

sourceAnchors.name: idea brokers
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar allows idea brokers as the chapter mechanism for moving patterns across contexts
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Idea brokers matter because they carry a working pattern out of one room and make it available to another problem.

sourceAnchors.name: creative desperation
sourceAnchors.detail: the source bundle permits creative desperation as deadline pressure that can force revision without guaranteeing creativity
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Creative desperation should feel like the moment the draft can no longer be protected by someday.

sourceAnchors.name: Disney's Frozen
sourceAnchors.detail: Frozen is named in the official source bundle as the innovation example, without support for detailed production chronology
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Frozen belongs as a narrow example of a creative work that needed borrowed patterns and hard revision to become coherent.

hook: Person at a meeting realizes the real lesson
The day starts with a dashboard
counterintuition: Productivity is not doing more faster
The problem is not effort but something deeper

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: a pediatric rehab clinic redesigning a boring home-exercise plan
exampleSpecs.audience: a therapist trying to keep children practicing between visits
exampleSpecs.stakes: patients stop doing exercises and recovery slows
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivia borrows progress-loop mechanics from a language-learning app and cuts every feature that does not help the child repeat the movement safely
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A foam balance pad squeaks under a child's sock

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional rail maintenance team reducing overnight inspection misses
exampleSpecs.audience: an engineer looking outside rail for inspection patterns
exampleSpecs.stakes: a missed coupling defect can cancel the morning schedule
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Etienne imports a pre-flight checklist pattern from aviation, then revises it around track access limits instead of copying it whole
exampleSpecs.firstImage: An empty platform hums under sodium lights after the last train leaves

exampleSpecs.domain: a food-truck owner rebuilding a lunch menu after sales stall
exampleSpecs.audience: an owner who confuses originality with refusing outside influence
exampleSpecs.stakes: another weak month could close the truck
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chidi accepts a queue-management idea from a pharmacy line and reshapes the menu board around faster choices
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "That line moves faster than ours," his sister says outside the pharmacy

exampleSpecs.domain: a city housing nonprofit revising an intake process under grant deadline pressure
exampleSpecs.audience: a program director whose team is protecting a clumsy draft
exampleSpecs.stakes: families will keep repeating the same story to three offices
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Laura until the grant deadline to stop defending the intake script and recombine a library reference-desk model with legal triage
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Laura two weeks of duplicate intake forms to admit the draft was not almost done

exampleSpecs.domain: an independent game studio trying to fix a tutorial that players skip
exampleSpecs.audience: a narrative designer under a demo deadline
exampleSpecs.stakes: players quit before learning the core mechanic
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marit tests a museum exhibit pattern, then cuts the clever narration that keeps players from touching the mechanic
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What if the best tutorial pattern is hiding in a children's museum exhibit?
mustAvoid: copying the museum format without revision

exampleSpecs.domain: a public defender office improving witness preparation without coaching testimony
exampleSpecs.audience: a training lead borrowing from sports practice design
exampleSpecs.stakes: witnesses either freeze or sound rehearsed in court
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Diego keep only the borrowed practice structure that preserves truthful recall, cutting anything that would make testimony sound scripted
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are in a windowless interview room with a legal pad turned sideways

skillTargets: identify when pressure enables revision rather than panic
choose outside patterns that fit the constraint instead of flattering novelty

tryThisNowSpec: Name one stuck problem, borrow one working pattern from a different field, and write the first constraint it must survive before you trust it.
